=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `plan()` returns an empty plan when `changed_files()` returns `None` for an empty, all-zero, or unreachable `--before`, so drift recovery never prepares the live copies on those pushes.
  WHY: The severity ranged from MAJOR to BLOCKER; using the highest, this can leave parity tests running against outdated templates and block integration.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The preparation step exits successfully when it skips processing due to a zero, empty, or unreachable `--before`, leaving no visible step-level signal that preparation was skipped.
  WHY: Severity ranged from NIT to MAJOR; using the highest, the skip can obscure why a later parity test fails.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: A branch-creation push can pass an all-zero `github.event.before` to the sync script, causing preparation to be skipped when the branch already contains template drift.
  WHY: The step stays green and parity tests can fail on that first push; the issue self-heals on a later push with a real `before`.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The comment claiming drift recovery works “whatever --before is” is inaccurate because recovery does not run when `--before` is empty, all-zero, or unreachable.
  WHY: The comment misleads maintainers about the conditions required for drift recovery.

- agents.md | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The documentation still describes parity preparation as applying only to PRs targeting `main`, despite the new preparation behavior for orchestrator integration PRs and pushes.
  WHY: Readers of the architecture reference get an inaccurate account of when and how the CI preparation step runs.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Document architectural changes in agents.md.
  expected_change_site: agents.md (via fragment)
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The PR adds triggers to ci.yml and updates README.md, but no fragment was added for agents.md to reflect that the CI pipeline now checks orchestrator integration branches.

- requirement: "Heal intake (`workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`) and `budget-watch` already act only on `main` pushes, and a new test pins that integration-branch pushes are not healed."
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py` (a `budget-watch`-gating test) or `tests/test_ci_budget_watch.py` (a new test that pins `budget-watch` skips pushes to `orchestrator/project-*`).
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The new `test_heal_intake_takes_ci_only_for_pushes_to_the_default_branch` covers the heal-intake branch but the PR description's "a new test pins that integration-branch pushes are not healed" claim is not backed by a parallel test for `budget-watch`. `ci.yml` line 1866 has the main-only `if: always() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` filter, but no test pins that filter against an `orchestrator/project-*` push event. With the new push trigger added to CI for those branches, a future change that loosens the `budget-watch` filter would not be caught.

- requirement: "The sync's drift recovery copies those too (template committed after its live copy), whatever --before is; a push has no PR base, so it passes its own before."
  expected_change_site: `scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py::plan()` and/or `.github/workflows/ci.yml` "Prepare template-only PR live copies for parity tests" step
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: When `--before` is the all-zero SHA on a branch-creation push, `changed_files()` returns `None` and `plan()` short-circuits to `[]` before the drift-recovery loop at `scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py:161-171` runs. There is no diff hunk in `sync_claude_live_copies.py` teaching `plan()` (or `changed_files()`) to fall through to the drift-recovery branch when `before` is zero / unreachable, and no diff hunk in `ci.yml` gates the prep step to skip branch-creation pushes or warns visibly when it does so. The PR description's "whatever --before is" promise is unfulfilled for the exact case the new push trigger creates.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Line or code reference: step "Prepare template-only PR live copies for parity tests", `--before "${PR_BASE_SHA:-${PUSH_BEFORE_SHA}}"`
  PROBLEM: A push that creates a new `orchestrator/project-*` branch has an all-zero `github.event.before`. That value goes to `sync_claude_live_copies.py`. There `changed_files()` (lines 133-144) returns None because the before SHA is all zeros (line 134). `plan()` then returns `[]` at lines 149-150, before the drift-recovery loop at lines 153-171 runs. So nothing is prepared on that push.
  WHY: The step stays green, and a force-push or any other unreachable `before` takes the same path. On a branch-creation push, if earlier merged sub-issue PRs left template-only changes without synced live copies, `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py` fails. The next push passes a real `before` and prepares correctly, so this self-heals. It only affects the first push of a branch and only when the branch already holds template drift. A fresh branch cut from `main` normally has none, because `main` is kept in step by the sync workflow.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Line or code reference: comment inside the same step, "The sync's drift recovery copies those too (template committed after its live copy), whatever --before is"
  PROBLEM: The comment overstates the behaviour. Drift recovery only runs when `--before` is a non-empty, non-zero, reachable commit. `changed_files()` returns None for an empty, all-zero or unreachable `--before`, and `plan()` then returns `[]` (scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py lines 134-150).
  WHY: This is documentation only. It misleads the next person debugging a `skip reason=no_before_commit` log line in a green step.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Line or code reference: same step, exit status after the sync script skips
  PROBLEM: When the script skips because `--before` is zero or unreachable, it logs `skip reason=no_before_commit` or `before_commit_unreachable` and exits 0. The step stays green with no step-level signal that preparation was skipped.
  WHY: A later parity-test failure on a branch-creation push has no visible cause at the step level. The skip is already logged by the script, so this is a diagnosability gap, not a correctness bug.

- agents.md | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  File: agents.md
  Line or code reference: lines 1603-1612, paragraph "For PRs targeting `main`, the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` CI job runs `sync_claude_live_copies.py sync --dry-run` ... Push CI and PRs targeting `stable` check the committed tree without preparation"
  PROBLEM: This PR changes the step's `if:` so preparation also runs for PRs into `orchestrator/project-*` and for pushes to `refs/heads/orchestrator/project-*`. Pushes use `github.event.before` as the base. `agents.md` still says only PRs targeting `main` are prepared and that push CI is unprepared. `agents.md` is not in the PR's changed files; only `README.md` was updated.
  WHY: This is documentation drift. `agents.md` is loaded as the architecture reference for the unattended pipelines, so the next reader gets a wrong picture of the parity-prep step.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  File: scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py
  Line or code reference: plan() function (approx lines 147-150) and calling site in .github/workflows/ci.yml
  PROBLEM: When a new branch is pushed (e.g., orchestrator/project-*), the PUSH_BEFORE_SHA is the all-zero SHA. The plan() function incorrectly short-circuits to return an empty list when changed_files() returns None for this SHA.
  WHY: The drift recovery (which syncs the templates) never runs for new integration branches, leaving parity tests running against outdated or mismatched templates.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Line or code reference: line 427
  PROBLEM: The comment states "The sync's drift recovery copies those too (template committed after its live copy), whatever --before is".
  WHY: This is factually incorrect when --before is an all-zero SHA, as shown by the logic short-circuit in scripts/sync_claude_live_copies.py.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  File: .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Line or code reference: Prepare template-only PR live copies for parity tests (lines 418-429)
  PROBLEM: The drift recovery step exits 0 even when it skips processing because of an invalid --before commit SHA.
  WHY: The CI job reports success (exit 0) even when the template synchronization did not actually occur, masking the issue and causing subsequent parity test failures to be attributed to the test code itself rather than the infra setup failure.
